R3B-moose-walk-0001.name: 3.5 km E of Spanish Creek
R3B-moose-walk-0001.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).

evidence.t: 42 wetlands within 2 km; nearest 0.9 ha, right here.
Cutblock harvested 2016 (10 years old), right here: browse.

seasonRows.notes: No row in the Region 5 table, so no general open season (page 5: open seasons are only those in the synopsis). Moose in Region 5: check the LEH synopsis.

plan: Drive: from Blue River, about 93 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Cedar St, Hwy 5, Lloyd Rd, E Old North Thompson Hwy.
Park: 52.00199, -120.32963, pull off on Spa151 (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk: 360 m N, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 14 m, about 9 min at 3 km/h.
Hunt: moose, season: VERIFY. Glass the wetland and cutblock edges at dawn and dusk. Move slowly, stop often (Tip).
Use: .308 Winchester, 165 to 180 grain premium bullet, shots inside about 200 m (219 yd) (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 5-15, Region 5. Season: no general open season (synopsis page 44, 95%). 1 legal flag below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-09, closures 2026-10-16.
R3B-moose-walk-0001.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 5-15: about 2,593 hunter days a year for moose (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.27 days per square km, middle third of BC MUs; access: average access. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).

tags.label: Good solo
tags.why: Short pack out: 0.4 km and about 14 m of climb from the parking (Tip). Cell coverage is not in the data: leave a trip plan and carry SOS or a satellite messenger (lesson: Bush safety).
